changes.rule_name: ERCOT Planning Guide, Section 9, Large Load Interconnection or Modification (Batch Zero)
changes.source_title: PUCT, Project No. 59142, Review of ERCOT's Interconnection Processes for Large Loads, Order Granting Good Cause Exceptions (item 53)
changes.what: After the Governor's directive of 3 August 2026, the PUCT granted ERCOT exceptions to Planning Guide 9.3.1(2)(a), 9.2.2(3)(a) and 5.3.5(5)(a)(ii): ERCOT may delay classifying Batch Zero Large Loads past the 7 August 2026 deadline, include eligible submitted base loads in the August and November 2026 QSAs, keep reviewing dynamic data after 7 August, and let ILLEs cure deficiencies within 24 days of notice.

cites.quote: Filed Date - 2026-08-20 12:29:32 PM Control Number - 59142 Item Number - 53
ORDER GRANTING GOOD CAUSE EXCEPTIONS
ERCOT Planning Guide § 9.3.1(2)(a) requires ERCOT to classify Large Loads as base load, studied load, or load that has not met sufficient criteria to be included in Batch Zero by August 7,2026
The exceptions permit ERCOT to delay classifying Large Loads for inclusion in Batch Zero
allow ILLEs to cure deficiencies within 24 days of notification

changes.license_basis: the Public Utility Commission of Texas's own copy on its Interchange (a commission record)
changes.notes: The registry step 9.3.1(2)(b) (Batch Zero study report by 9 April 2027) is not changed by this order; ERCOT's deck of 14-15 September (next entry) says the effect on that date is still being determined.

changes.rule_name: ERCOT Batch Zero large load study (PGRR 145)
changes.source_title: ERCOT, Item 14: Batch Zero Update, Board of Directors Meeting, September 14-15, 2026
changes.what: ERCOT gave the Interconnecting TSPs a provisional (conditional) Batch Zero classification of each Large Load on 3 September 2026 (PGRR 145 had set 7 August 2026 for the final one): 204 projects (66.4 GW) as base load and 158 (127.9 GW) as studied load; final inclusion waits on the eligibility verification and audit, whose report is due to the PUCT by 10 December 2026, and energization of new Large Load data centers and crypto mining facilities is paused until then.

cites.quote: 204 projects (66.4 GW) met the qualifications to be conditionally included as base load
158 projects (127.9 GW) met the qualifications to be conditionally included as studied load

cites.section: Key Changes to Batch Zero, item 4
cites.quote: to the Interconnecting TSPs on September 3, 2026

cites.section: Key Changes to Batch Zero, item 4
cites.quote: (Originally, PGRR 145 required ERCOT to provide final classification on August 7, 2026.)

cites.section: Key Changes to Batch Zero, item 1
cites.quote: ERCOT will file the Batch Zero Eligibility Verification Report with the Commission by December 10, 2026

cites.section: Key Changes to Batch Zero, item 3
cites.quote: ERCOT has paused the energization of new Large Load data centers and crypto mining facilities

cites.section: Key Changes to Batch Zero, item 5
cites.quote: Originally, PGRR 145 required ERCOT to complete the study by April 9. 2027.

cites.section: Attachment A, Concluding the Verification Process (ERCOT letter of November 4, 2026)
cites.quote: ERCOT must complete its review this month to file a report with the PUCT on December 10, 2026.

changes.license_basis: ERCOT's own copy under www.ercot.com/files (robots allow; ERCOT's terms allow reuse in compilations and analyses); the November letter is the PUCT's copy
changes.notes: The deck's chart legend prints the studied total as 125.4 GW (158 projects) where its key takeaways print 127.9 GW; the takeaway is quoted, the difference is the deck's. ERCOT's letter of 4 November 2026 also says it will file further good cause exception requests for the PUCT's 17 December 2026 open meeting.

changes.rule_name: NPRR1348, Telemetry Offsetting for Provisional Controllable Load Resources
changes.source_title: ERCOT, Nodal Protocol Revision Requests, Pending NPRRs report
changes.what: A market participant (Global Capacity Alliance) filed NPRR1348, which would let a QSE raise the telemetered Low Power Consumption limit of a Provisional Controllable Load Resource (the flexible-load path of the large load process) to match a paired resource; it is pending, not approved.

cites.quote: Telemetry Offsetting for Provisional Controllable Load Resources
It permits a Qualified Scheduling Entity (QSE) to dynamically raise the telemetered Low Power Consumption (LPC) limit of a Provisional Controllable Load Resource (PCLR)
Global Capacity Alliance

changes.rule_name: CAISO, Large Load Enhancements (response to FERC's Order to Show Cause, EL26-71)
changes.source_title: CAISO news release, CAISO Board advances new procedures for connecting large loads quickly and reliably, 10/28/2026
changes.what: The CAISO Board of Governors approved the large load proposal (a flexible interim load interconnection with enforceable flexibility until network upgrades are complete, and a monthly window to review out-of-cycle transmission upgrades for large loads to fit the PTOs' 60 to 90 day studies); the CAISO will file it with FERC by 16 November 2026.

cites.quote: With the Board’s approval Wednesday, the ISO will file its proposal with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) by its November 16 deadline.

referred to as a “flexible interim load interconnection,” would enable large loads to interconnect quickly to the transmission system with enforceable flexibility determined by grid conditions and constraints until associated network upgrades are complete
the proposal creates a new monthly window for the ISO to review any transmission additions or upgrades associated with large loads that fall outside the usual transmission planning cycle
Oct 28, 2026 Board of Governors approval
Nov 16, 2026 FERC filing
Docket No. EL26-71-000

changes.license_basis: the CAISO's own site (robots allow; the CAISO's terms allow use with the CAISO credited)
changes.notes: No Board memo or minutes for 28 October were read; the CAISO's process page also lists second revised draft tariff language of 30 October 2026 (with ride-through provisions), not read here.

changes.rule_name: PJM Tariff definition of Large Load and Large Load Registry (ER26-3515)
changes.source_title: FERC, Order Accepting Tariff Revisions in Part and Rejecting Tariff Revisions in Part, PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Docket No. ER26-3515-000, 197 FERC 61,019 (issued October 9, 2026), as PJM posts it
changes.what: FERC accepted PJM's Tariff definition of Large Load (end-use load with a cumulative peak of 50 MW or more at a single electrical site behind one or more points of interconnection, affiliated facilities within one mile counted as one site) and a Large Load Registry, effective 12 October 2026, with a compliance filing due in 30 days, and rejected the rest of PJM's filing (IRAS, the new-capacity requirement, BYONC and the VRR exclusion).

cites.quote: (Issued October 9, 2026)

we accept PJM’s proposed Tariff revisions to establish a definition of Large Load and a Large Load Registry, effective October 12, 2026, as requested, and require PJM to submit a compliance filing within 30 days of the date of issuance of this order
We reject PJM’s remaining proposed Tariff revisions
end-use customer(s) load that has a cumulative peak load of 50 [MW] or greater at a single electrical site behind one or more points of interconnection
We find that PJM’s proposed definition of Large Load is just and reasonable and not unduly discriminatory or preferential.

changes.license_basis: PJM's own posted copy (www.pjm.com, robots allow); a FERC order is a federal work
changes.notes: The registry file holds the PJM Board's proposed definition of January 2026 (at or above 50 MW at a single Point of Interconnection); the accepted Tariff definition counts a cumulative peak at a single electrical site. The order does not say the filing came from the CIFP. Whether PJM made the 30-day compliance filing was not read.
